solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Game that's bound to frustrate

parts.note: to bound is to leap, or hop
to scotch a plan is to thwart or frustrate it

explanation.surface: A pastime whose very purpose is to thwart whoever plays it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is a link. 'Bound' looks like 'certain to', but it is the leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Hopscotch is a children's playground game of hopping between chalked squares.

clue.text: Unpopular form of death

indicators.note: a form of a word is a reshaped version of it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dying in a way that nobody approves of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' turns DEATH into a new arrangement of its five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hated is disliked by others, which is to say thoroughly unpopular.

clue.text: Ruth takes in lake and river somewhere in Scotland

indicators.note: taking in something means holding it within, so one piece encloses the others

parts.note: ruth is an old word for compassion, or pity
loch is the Scottish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A woman called Ruth tours a Scottish lake and river on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name but is an old noun for compassion; 'takes in' wraps it round the lake and river.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitlochry is a Highland town in Perthshire, so it is indeed a place in Scotland.

clue.text: Arachnid in Gloucester? See the mice run!

indicators.note: the mice run about, scattering the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm as rodents scurry around a West Country city.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloucester is not the city but a cheese (Double Gloucester), the home of this tiny mite. 'run' shuffles SEE THE MICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheese mite is a minute arachnid infesting cheese, such as a Gloucester, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Mo was first to be amused

parts.note: a mo is a moment, as is a tick, both informal British words for a short time
someone who was first in a race led it

explanation.surface: A person named Mo is delighted to have come first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mo' looks like a name; it is the British 'half a mo', a moment. 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickled, in the sense of tickled pink, means pleased or amused.

clue.text: Poor man's refuge? Heart of Midlothian

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter, a refuge

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part, here the two middle letters

explanation.surface: A football fan seeks shelter in a Scottish stadium; Heart of Midlothian is an Edinburgh football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Midlothian (Hearts) is a Scottish football club; here 'Heart of' takes OT, the middle of MIDLOTHIAN. The 's of 'man's' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-not is a poor person, one without wealth, as in the haves and the have-nots.

clue.text: Malaysian state in which Abraham's wife has change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart here means the central letter of the name is swapped for another

parts.note: in the Bible Abraham's wife is Sarah

explanation.surface: A biblical matriarch changes her mind about something in Southeast Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has change of heart' replaces the middle R of SARAH with B. 'in which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabah is a state of Malaysia in the north of Borneo.

clue.text: Card game providing something for one to do

definitions.meaning: ... whist is a card game in which a player may play alone against the others
a performance by a single person, unaccompanied

explanation.definitionFit: Solo names both a whist-like card game and a piece performed by a single person alone.

clue.text: Worker taps tree

parts.note: a worker bee is the commonest crossword worker
taps are marked C and H, for cold and hot

explanation.surface: A labourer draws sap from a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taps' seems a verb; it is the pair of basin taps marked C (cold) and H (hot).
explanation.definitionFit: The beech is a common broadleaf tree with smooth grey bark.

clue.text: Your turn to support partner in farm management

indicators.note: in a down clue the support goes underneath, so this piece comes below the other

parts.note: a husband is a spouse or partner

indicators.note: a turn means the short form for your is read backwards

explanation.surface: Telling someone it is their go to back up their spouse in running the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses YR to RY, and 'to support' puts it below HUSBAND in this down entry. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandry is the care of crops and livestock, the practice of farming.

clue.text: In court it legally established claim to ownership

indicators.note: in means the answer sits inside the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A judge decides who legally owns something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'established' is a link joining the run to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A title in law is the right to own property, or a document evidencing that right.

clue.text: They find fault with traffic skirting French town

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge of, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: traffic is made up of cars
ville is French for town

explanation.surface: Grumblers moan about the cars going round a town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirting' wraps the traffic round the French town. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavillers raise petty objections, quibblers who find fault.

clue.text: Work to get solution after doctor writes

indicators.note: after places the work and solution behind the doctor

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
saline is a salt solution used in medicine

explanation.surface: A medical patient awaits a solution once the doctor has written a prescription.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link. The surface of a drip in hospital hides an idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a line is to write a short letter, so it is a phrase for writes.

clue.text: How runaway is brought to a stop?

indicators.note: a runaway has escaped control, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Asking how a bolting horse can be halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runaway' rearranges HOW to WHO; 'is brought to' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoa is the call to a horse to halt, an instruction to stop.

clue.text: Too far away from the Pennines, say?

definitions.meaning: beyond reach, as a target too distant to hit
the Pennines are a range of hills in northern England, so leaving them is departing a range

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means too distant to reach, and also, playfully, having left a mountain range.

clue.text: Former philosopher's daughter brought to light

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
David Hume was the Scottish philosopher
D is the abbreviation for daughter in genealogy

explanation.surface: An old thinker's daughter is revealed to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhume is to dig up, so something exhumed has been unearthed and revealed.

clue.text: Novel sensation for Russian neighbours

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A book causing a stir among those living next to Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' seems to be a book; it signals rearranging SENSATION. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonians live in Estonia, which borders Russia, so they are its neighbours.

clue.text: Bound to believe what one hears?

indicators.note: what one hears points to the sound of a word rather than its spelling

parts.note: to trust is to believe in

explanation.surface: Obliged to accept whatever one is told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' first reads as 'certain to'; 'Bound' is the definition and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means tied up tightly, as a chicken is bound before roasting.

clue.text: Working girl has an earthly paradise

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A girl in employment finds heaven on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Shangri-La is the idyllic Himalayan valley of James Hilton's novel, a byword for utopia.

clue.text: Be audacious with satellite carrying ultimate in technology

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Being bold with a high-tech satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts Y, the end of 'technology', inside TRITON. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is a British idiom for being cheeky or testing limits, an act of audacity.

clue.text: Pacific islander about the same

indicators.note: the letters read about, from the other end, come out the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A Pacific person who is much like the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads identically in both directions, which 'about the same' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nauruan comes from Nauru, a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: Irregularity when end of December is ignored in a typical year

indicators.note: something ignored is left out, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: normal means typical

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Something odd happens when the last of December goes unnoticed in an ordinary year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is ignored' removes R, the end of December, from NORMAL. 'when' and 'in' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly is a deviation from the norm, an irregularity.

clue.text: In a month people must replace us? Swell!

indicators.note: replacing means one part is swapped out for another

parts.note: August is a month
taken as written
men are people

explanation.surface: Excited exclamation about crowds displacing us in some month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must replace' swaps the US of AUGUST for MEN. 'In a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell something is to enlarge it, and augment is to increase, a synonym.

clue.text: Appropriate name for the Devil

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to take for oneself, to steal

explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for stealing, and Old Nick is a nickname for the Devil.

clue.text: Pierce one's skin

parts.note: to cut is to pierce
one is I, and one's is read as I is, giving IS

explanation.surface: Puncturing someone's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical Latin term for the skin.

clue.text: Move Central American fish or bird

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly

indicators.note: central means the middle letters of the next word

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A choice between moving a fish or a bird in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central American' looks like a region; 'Central' takes RI, the middle of AMERICAN. 'or' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet, a bird often kept as a pet.

clue.text: Old magistrate about to meet first offender

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Eve was the first sinner, eating the forbidden fruit

explanation.surface: A historic judge is about to face a criminal on their first offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first offender' looks like a newcomer to crime; it is Eve, first to sin. 'to meet' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval English official with local judicial powers, a magistrate of old.

clue.text: Lacking substance, feature of the Blair years

indicators.note: feature of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political jibe that Tony Blair's time as prime minister was all spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was UK prime minister from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy can mean insubstantial or flimsy, like a vague promise.

clue.text: Assign property

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to credit something to a source
as a noun, a quality or characteristic

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to ascribe; as a noun, a quality something possesses.

clue.text: Rumour is beginning to escalate after denial

indicators.note: after places these letters behind the denial

parts.note: no is a denial

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Gossip starts to spread after someone denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise in the old sense is talk or rumour, as in a story noised abroad.

clue.text: Crack troops stay outside being cheeky

parts.note: the SAS is Britain's elite Special Air Service regiment

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers stand guard outdoors while being impudent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' takes S and Y, the outer letters of 'stay'. 'being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sassy is informal for impudent or saucy, a synonym for cheeky.

clue.text: Tate Modern not the first new cathedral

indicators.note: new means the letters are put into a new arrangement
not the first means the opening letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A London gallery reinvented as a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is a London art gallery. 'not the first' drops T from Tate, and 'new' rearranges ATE MODERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the famous Gothic cathedral in Paris.
